messages:
liam: FYI I'm seeing inconsistent auth when spinning up >1 AsyncClient in the same process. One client sometimes sends the other client's API key.

kate: ouch. can you share a tiny repro? sounds like a shared transport/auth cache.

liam: minimal test (uses fake network layer):
```py
import asyncio
from redwood import AsyncClient

async def run(key):
    c = AsyncClient(api_key=key)
    res = await c._send_raw('ping')  # internal test hook
    print(key, res.headers.get('x-used-key'))

async def main():
    await asyncio.gather(run('K1'), run('K2'))

asyncio.run(main())
```
Sometimes output: K1 K1
K2 K1  # second task used K1. intermittent.

emily: thanks. Do you set REDWOOD_API_KEY in env or pass provider objects? precedence bugs happen when constructor defers to a module-level provider.

liam: no env var in this test. Passing api_key into constructor should take precedence.

rory: check whether AsyncClient reuses a module-level Transport or AuthAdapter. If an AuthAdapter has a cached token stored on the adapter instance and that instance is shared, you get this symptom.

kate: can you inspect id(c._auth_adapter) and id(c._transport) before the call? Also try creating clients with client_id kwarg and log it in headers to see mapping.

liam: did that: both clients return the same auth_adapter id in failing runs. Looks like factory does memoization keyed only on config hash which collides.

emily: two asks: 1) immediate mitigation: document that concurrent AsyncClient instances should be created with separate transports or use \"async with AsyncClient(... )\" which will ensure instance-scoped adapters, 2) longer-term: remove memoization for stateful adapters or key them by client identity.

rory: developer experience suggestion: add an explicit param bind_credentials=True and an async context manager so sample code encourages scoping creds. e.g.
```py
async with AsyncClient(api_key='K1', bind_credentials=True) as c:
    await c.generate('...')
```
This also reads nicely in notebooks.

kate: typing note: our __init__ accepts credentials: Any. We should add a TypedAuthProvider Protocol and annotate AsyncClient to accept AuthProvider | str for api_key to catch misuse. Also helpful to add a small lint rule example in devex docs.

liam: I'll write a failing pytest that asserts unique header per concurrent call and attach to the issue.

emily: can we also tweak quickstart to spell the precedence order (constructor api_key > explicit AuthProvider instance > REDWOOD_API_KEY env var) and call out that provider instances may be stateful and should not be shared across clients?

kate: agreed. I'll draft a short FAQ blurb and a code snippet to recommend using context manager.

devex-bot: Created issue #4170: \"async: Auth adapter memoization causes multi-client key bleed\" - https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/4170 :memo: Labels: devex, bug, needs-test.

rory: follow-ups for eng: 1) change memoization to either be stateless-only or include client-id in key, 2) add bind_credentials/context manager, 3) add TypedAuthProvider Protocol + examples.

liam: thanks everyone, will post the pytest and a short log snippet in the issue. appreciate the quick triage. :rocket:
